description_full: Renishaw plc, an engineering and scientific technology company, designs, manufactures, distributes, sells, and services technological products and services, and analytical instruments and medical devices worldwide. The company operates through three segments: Industrial Metrology, Position Measurement, and Specialised Technologies. It offers precision measurement and process control products, such as co-ordinate measuring machine probes, software, retrofits, equator gauging systems, fixtures, machine calibration and optimization, machine tool probes, precision styli for metrology, and smart manufacturing data platform; and position and motion control products comprising interferometric laser, magnetic, and optical encoders. The company also provides healthcare products, such as neuromate stereotactic robots, neuroinfuse drug delivery systems, neuroinspire surgical planning software, dixi medical's, and Raman spectrometers; industrial robots; and metal additive 3D printing manufacturing systems. It serves the aerospace, automotive, consumer electronics, medical and healthcare, heavy, machine builder, energy, and precision manufacturing industries, as well as scientific, research, and analysis industries. The company was incorporated in 1973 and is based in Wotton-under-Edge, the United Kingdom.

financial_summary: Renishaw Plc is a mid-cap technology business with a $5.2B market cap on $1.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 10% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 46%.

The business throws off $82M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.93× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.5%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 52% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

AI disruption of existing software moats — incumbents with durable margins face commoditisation as AI-native competitors replicate features at a fraction of the R&D cost.
Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 9.7%, but the 4pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.18).
